events.description: 8. ORDER: The undersigned panel, appointed by the Chief Judge of the United States Fifth Circuit Court of Appeal, is taking the issue of its jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 2284 under advisement. Pending the panel's examination of jurisdiction: IT IS ORDERED that the defendants shall file any opposition to the plaintiff's claim for injunctive relief on or before May 5th, 2026; IT IS ORDERED that the plaintiffs shall file a brief in response to the defendant's Motion to Transfer (Rec Doc. 6) on or before May 5th, 2026; IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the plaintiffs are granted leave to file a reply to the defendant's opposition, and the defendants are granted leave to file a reply to the plaintiff's opposition to transfer on or before May 7th, 2026. This matter will be set for hearing by separate notice. The parties are ORDERED to state in their respective briefs whether an evidentiary hearing is requested. If no evidence is to be offered this matter will be deemed submitted on the briefs. Issued on behalf of the panel. Signed by Chief Judge Shelly D. Dick on 5/1/2026. (SWE) (Entered: 05/01/2026)

events.description: 25. RULING: Because Plaintiffs do not raise a direct challenge to the apportionment of any congressional districts, and do not provide any alternative grounds under § 2284, their Motion to Convene a Three-Judge District Court is DENIED for want of jurisdiction as stated herein. Signed by Stuart Kyle Duncan, Circuit Judge, Greg Guidry, District Judge and Shelly D. Dick, District Judge on 5/8/2026. (SWE) Modified on 5/8/2026 (SWE).

events.description: 26. RULING AND ORDER: For the foregoing reasons, Defendants' 6 Motion to Transfer Venue is GRANTED. It is therefore ORDERED that the above-captioned case shall be TRANSFERRED in its entirety to the Western District of Louisiana. The Clerk of this Court shall take such steps as are needed to effectuate this transfer. Signed by Chief Judge Shelly D. Dick on 5/8/2026. (SWE) (Entered: 05/08/2026)
